claims.text: Low to moderate Al additions up to approximately 5 at.% promote local chemical short-range order in CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
Low to moderate Al additions enhance lattice distortion in CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
Al-induced short-range order and lattice distortion enhance dislocation mobility.
Al-induced short-range order and lattice distortion promote transformation-induced plasticity.
Transformation-induced plasticity and enhanced dislocation mobility maintain or slightly improve toughness at Al concentrations up to approximately 5 at.%.
Above approximately 5 at.% Al, coarse B2-ordered precipitates form.
The B2-ordered precipitates formed at high Al content are brittle.
Coarse B2 precipitates concentrate stress at phase boundaries.
Stress concentration and impeded dislocation motion caused by B2 precipitates lead to premature fracture and reduced toughness.
The significant formation of deleterious B2 precipitates begins above a critical concentration of approximately 5 at.% Al.
Relative to the near-zero-Al baseline, toughness will be maintained or slightly improved at Al levels of 5 at.% or less.
Toughness will drop sharply when Al content exceeds approximately 5 at.%.
Toughness will follow a bell-shaped trend as a function of Al concentration over the investigated range.
The proposed behavior is bounded to approximately 0–10 at.% Al under arc melting, solution treatment near 1100°C, rapid quenching, and aging at 600°C for 2 hours.
Processing changes or compositions outside the stated range may produce different microstructural evolution and mechanical properties.
